Tedious

TEE-dee-us — think of the weary sigh of 'te-di-um'; a tedious task feels like it drags on forever. · adjective

Hear It

What It Means

Tedious is boring, tiresome, or monotonous.

Filling out the same form over and over made the tedious paperwork feel like it would never end.

Worked Example

A volunteer spends an entire afternoon typing the same five pieces of information from three thousand handwritten donation cards into a spreadsheet, one card at a time, with no variation from the first card to the last.

That repetitive, drawn-out task with no excitement or variety is exactly what tedious means. Unlike 'difficult,' which means hard to do, tedious specifically means boring because of how repetitive or long it is.

How Tedious Sits Among Its Neighbors

Synonyms — open each to see how it differs

monotonous

monotonous: dull and repetitive, lacking variety

tiresome

tiresome: causing weariness or boredom

dull

dull: lacking interest or excitement

Antonyms

exciting

exciting: causing great enthusiasm or interest

engaging

engaging: holding someone's attention pleasantly

How Strong Is It? — dull → tedious → monotonous

dull vs. tedious

dull vs. tedious: Dull is a milder, more general word than tedious -- something dull might just lack excitement briefly, while tedious specifically emphasizes a long, repetitive process that feels like it drags on.

monotonous vs. tedious

monotonous vs. tedious: Monotonous can feel even flatter than tedious: monotonous specifically emphasizes repeating the exact same thing over and over, while tedious can describe any long, boring task, repetitive or not.

Build the Word

The pieces

root — taed-

root — taed-: weariness, disgust (Latin (taedium, taedere))

Put it together

Put it together: Latin taedium meant 'weariness, boredom, disgust.' Tedious, at its root, describes exactly that feeling of dragging weariness brought on by something long and repetitive.

Use the root in a new word: tedium

Use the root in a new word: tedium: The tedium of the long car ride was broken only by a few short rest stops.
